svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "The three states of matter as particles."], [1, "Solid: particles vibrate in fixed positions."], [3, "Liquid: particles move past each other."], [5, "Gas: particles move fast and far apart."], [7.5, "Changes of state: energy in to melt, boil or sublime; energy out to freeze, condense or deposit."], [11, "Entropy increases from solid to liquid to gas."]]
svg.title: States of matter
svg.desc: Particle diagrams of a solid with vibrating particles in a lattice, a liquid with particles moving past each other and a gas with fast, widely spaced particles, with changes of state and increasing entropy.
svg.text: States of matter: the particle model
Each circle is a particle (atom or molecule).

g.data-info: Particles in fixed positions in a regular arrangement, vibrating. Fixed shape and volume.
Particles close together but able to move past each other. Fixed volume; takes the shape of its container.
Particles far apart, moving fast and randomly. Fills its container; easily compressed.
Melting, boiling and sublimation need energy (endothermic); freezing, condensing and deposition release it (exothermic).
Entropy (disorder) increases from solid to liquid to gas, as the particles become more dispersed.
